findings.element: [data-app="notes"] [data-act="send"] — the seam's primary act, and the .peel footer row
findings.problem: Clear the wording field (.peelField) — the ordinary retype gesture — and the one act the suite exists to perform becomes a lie. _gate-suite.html:19388 runs send.toggleAttribute("aria-disabled", !ready), which writes the EMPTY STRING; aria-disabled="" is an invalid token, so Chromium falls back to false and Playwright's accessibility snapshot returns {"role":"button","name":"Write the wording, then send"} with no disabled state. Because "" never matches [aria-disabled="true"], the Notes shell's own guards at :5680-5683 (ink-3 colour, cursor: default) stop applying: measured bg rgb(17,17,17), colour rgb(255,255,255), cursor pointer, opacity 1, pointer-events auto — a full-ink primary pill. Clicking it or pressing Enter does nothing: 13 cards before, 13 after, #say silent, peel still open, focus unmoved. First paint is correct (:18076 emits aria-disabled="true"); only the live typing path lies, which is why no static sweep catches it. The label swap then rewraps the footer: send goes [596,591,138,36] -> [272,635,227,36] (324px left, 44px down) while "Never mind" goes [491,591] -> [637,591] — 146px RIGHT, landing inside the rectangle Send occupied a frame earlier (both right edges at x=734). True at 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920. Select-all, delete, reach back to where Send was, and you press the control that throws the peel away.
findings.fix: At :19388 replace send.toggleAttribute("aria-disabled", !ready) with send.setAttribute("aria-disabled", ready ? "false" : "true") so the a11y tree and the [aria-disabled="true"] CSS guards both fire. Stop swapping the button's own text: keep it reading "Send to Tasks" at its 138px width in every state, and render "Write the wording, then send" as a hint line under .peelField instead, so the footer row never rewraps and "Never mind" never slides into the slot the primary act just vacated.

findings.element: [data-app="timeline"] .b-edit on the ACROSS desk (the default layout), opened by .b-grab or by [data-act="add"]
findings.problem: Round 6 moved the editor out from between the horizon and the track so the grab handles stop being pushed off screen; it now opens after the plan and lands below the fold. Measured after a full 1.4s settle: .b-grab at 1440x960 gives [196,859,1130,554] — 101px of a 554px pane visible, 0 of 4 steppers on screen, first stepper 146px below the viewport bottom. At 1440x1000 [196,899,1130,554], 101px. At 1920x1000 [196,899,1610,554], 101px. At 1280x900 [196,895,970,554] — FIVE pixels visible. Via "Add a moment" at 1440x1000, 28px visible. Pressing "Edit Send the invitations" at 1280x900 paints a faint wash behind one label and scrolls the sheet 173px: the person's place moves and the thing they opened never arrives. Keyboard users recover on the next Tab via native focus scroll; pointer users get nothing. keepInBand (:21926) does exactly what it says — it keeps the MOMENT'S ROW in the band — and nothing ever puts .b-edit in the band. The behaviour gate cannot see it: across @w · placing a moment is not done blind (:875) asserts .b-grab handles stay visible, never the editor. The DOWN layout is correct: [227,615,344,554], 345px visible, 4 of 4 steppers on screen.
findings.fix: In keepInBand, when root.querySelector(".b-edit") exists and the band resolved to the .app.sheet scroller (the !fixed && !paneScrolls branch), run the existing minimum-correction arithmetic on the PANEL instead of the moment's row: top = panel.getBoundingClientRect().top - box.getBoundingClientRect().top and height = panel.getBoundingClientRect().height, keeping the same pad = 24 and the too-tall re-centre fallback. Verified by hand: scrolling the band so .b-edit's bottom sits 24px inside the viewport puts all 4 steppers on screen and still leaves 6 of 7 grab handles visible at 1280x1000 and 7 of 7 at 1440x1000 and 1920x1000 — comfortably above the gate's >= 1.

findings.element: [data-act="projects"] (the project switcher listbox) and [data-rail="more"] (the spine's More menu) — both suite-level objects
findings.problem: Four popups in one application, driven identically at 1440x960 (focus opener, Enter, ArrowDown, ArrowDown, Escape), and two of the four have no keyboard model behind what they advertise. Show (menu, 14 items) puts focus in the menu, walks it with arrows and returns focus to "Show" on Escape. The card Move menu (menu, 5 items) does the same and returns focus to the card. The project switcher ships aria-haspopup="listbox", flips aria-expanded to "true" and paints a real role="listbox" aria-label "Projects" with four role="option"s — then leaves focus on the opener, sets no aria-activedescendant, no aria-controls, and ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End do nothing at all; its options are reachable only by Tab. The rail's More menu declares role="menu" with three items, leaves focus on the opener, and the rail's own roving arrow handler eats the keys, so ArrowDown inside an open menu moves the rail tile UNDER it ("Settings", then "Orla, venue manager") and Escape abandons focus on that tile rather than on "More". Separately, Tab from inside the open card Move menu lands on <body> while .cardMenu is still painted over the board.
findings.fix: Give both objects the model Show already implements in this same file. Project switcher: on Enter/Space/ArrowDown move focus to the currently selected [role="option"], let Up/Down/Home/End walk the options, Enter choose, Escape close and return focus to the opener; add aria-controls on the opener pointing at the listbox id. Rail More: while moreOpen is true, return early from the rail's roving arrow handler and hand Up/Down/Home/End to the three .moreItem buttons, with Escape closing and focusing [data-rail="more"]. Card Move menu: on Tab, close .cardMenu and move focus to the control after [data-act="menu"] rather than letting focus fall to the body with the menu still open.

findings.element: [data-app="notes"] — the repaint that runs when the notebook crosses 720px
findings.problem: Focus a Notes control, narrow one page past 720, widen it back. [data-act="review"] (.idxGo, "Go through the 8 notes still to decide."), [data-act="photo"] and the seam's own [data-act="send"] all exist and are visible on BOTH sides of the crossing, and all three end on <body> at 390 and are still on <body> after widening back to 1440. Nothing announces the loss; the next Tab restarts at the top of the document. .topField survives because it is a TEXTAREA. Cause is exact: the Notes repaint (~:19100) captures the index scroll, the read-body scroll and a caret, but only if (active.tagName === "TEXTAREA" || active.tagName === "INPUT"); mount.innerHTML = ... at :19143 then destroys every button. Same-band resizes (1440->1400->1300) and the 1199 crossing all hold focus, so this is the 720 repaint specifically. Tasks holds focus across the same crossing both ways (checked on a card and on the dock search field) and Timeline lands it on a real heading — Notes alone drops it. The gate cannot see it: ${product} · crossing 720 both ways throws nothing (:1467) asserts layout, toggles, lanes, rows, sideways scroll and console noise, never document.activeElement.
findings.fix: In the same capture block, when active is not a field, also record { act: active.dataset.act, role: active.getAttribute("aria-label") } — both are stable across the breakpoint even where the class name changes (.verb -> .dockGlyph). After mount.innerHTML is written, re-find it with mount.querySelector('[data-act="' + act + '"]'), confirm its aria-label matches the recorded role, and call .focus({ preventScroll: true }). This is the selector-then-role rule Notes already runs for fields, extended from fields to controls.

findings.element: [data-app="notes"] review — the "Delete it everywhere?" two-step confirm (.confirm, [data-act="d-delete-yes"|"d-delete-no"])
findings.problem: Press Delete on a review card: the confirm comes up, #say reads "Delete this note? ... You can undo this for 30 seconds.", focus lands on "Keep it". Escape, Enter and Space behave, and 'd' is correctly a no-op. But with the confirm still up, 't' silently replaces it with the SEND peel and drops focus into the wording textarea — the pending delete gone with nothing said; 'k' silently FILES the note and advances the queue 1 of 8 -> 2 of 8 ("Kept in Notes. 7 left."); 'l' silently defers it and moves to the next note. So the person who asked to delete a note and then touched one letter has committed a different decision on that same note and moved on. The source comment at :20166 says "Delete stays keycap-free behind its two-step confirm" — the confirm does not hold the keyboard, so it is not one. The confirm also carries role="status" rather than role="alertdialog", has no aria-modal, and Tab from "Keep it" walks straight out of it — index row, dock search, account tile, body, then round to the rail — eight stops without ever returning to either answer.
findings.fix: confirming (:18634) is already the flag. In the keydown handler, immediately after if (typing) return; at :20153 — above the '/' search branch, the t/k/l branch at :20161 and the ["ArrowDown","ArrowUp","j","k"] branch at :20187 — add if (state === "review" && confirming) return; so a pending destructive confirm owns the keyboard and only Escape and the two answers' own Enter/Space reach anything. Then change the .confirm span from role="status" to role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true" with an accessible name, and cycle Tab between its two buttons.

biggestWin: The reversibility model. Every act I could find that changes something announces itself in one voice, hands the keyboard somewhere sensible, and can be taken back: the keyboard carry says "Picked up ...", then "In progress, position 1 of 4.", and Escape says "Move cancelled. ... is back in the to do column." and really puts it back; the seam sends, lands focus on "Open in Tasks", crosses to Tasks with focus on the card that landed, and Ctrl+Z from the room it sent you to says "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks."; a tick in the 32-task dense board keeps its lane at scrollTop 251, follows focus to Done, and restores both on undo. And the overdue filter is the cleanest thing here — it states itself ("Showing 1 overdue task. 12 others are hidden."), keeps the head's counts honest while it hides things, and when the last overdue task is ticked it releases itself and says why: "Nothing is overdue, so the filter is off." That is the dead-end-filter class from the paid-for library closed properly rather than patched.
